title: Karnataka Mango Corporation to Build Dedicated Platform for Alphonso Domestic Sales
excerpt: The Karnataka State Mango Development and Marketing Corporation plans to create a specialized digital platform to boost domestic marketing of Alphonso mangoes, building on its existing Karsiri portal infrastructure.
body:
• Karnataka's mango corporation (KSMDMC) is developing a dedicated digital platform to strengthen domestic marketing of Alphonso mangoes grown in the state.
  • The initiative builds on the existing Karsiri portal, which already connects farmers directly with consumers for 12 mango varieties across Karnataka.
  • Karnataka is among India's top mango-producing states, with cultivation spread across districts including Kolar, Dharwad, and Ramanagara.
  • The move aims to help farmers secure better prices while reducing reliance on middlemen in the Alphonso supply chain.

A New Push for Karnataka's Alphonso Growers

The Karnataka State Mango Development and Marketing Corporation (KSMDMC) is set to develop a specialized platform for the domestic marketing of Alphonso mangoes, according to The Hindu. The initiative marks the corporation's latest effort to strengthen direct sales channels for one of India's most prized mango varieties, which has traditionally been associated with Maharashtra's Konkan belt but is also cultivated across several Karnataka districts.

KSMDMC, a Government of Karnataka enterprise under the Department of Horticulture established in 2011, has been steadily expanding its digital infrastructure to connect mango farmers with consumers. The new platform would focus specifically on Alphonso — known locally as Badami in parts of Karnataka — and aims to create a more organized domestic supply chain for the premium fruit.

Building on the Karsiri Foundation

The corporation already operates the Karsiri portal (karsirimangoes.karnataka.gov.in), a direct-to-consumer marketplace launched in 2018 that offers 12 mango varieties including Alphonso, Kesar, Himam Pasand, Mallika, Neelam, Malgova, and Totapuri. The portal, run in collaboration with India Post, allows farmers to pack and ship mangoes directly to consumers through the General Post Office network, cutting out traditional intermediaries.

Karsiri has seen varying volumes over the years. In 2021, the India Post partnership delivered 75 tonnes of mangoes; in 2022, that figure was 70 tonnes, according to Krishi Jagran. The service has expanded beyond Bengaluru to cover 31 PIN codes across Karnataka, including Hubballi-Dharwad, Mysuru, Belagavi, Mangaluru, and Hassan.

The new Alphonso-focused platform appears designed to go beyond what Karsiri currently offers, creating targeted marketing infrastructure for a variety that commands premium prices and faces stiff competition from established Konkan-origin Alphonso brands.

Why Alphonso, and Why Now

Alphonso mangoes occupy a unique position in India's fruit economy. While Maharashtra's Ratnagiri and Devgad districts dominate the market — with GI-tagged Alphonso commanding prices that can exceed ₹1,000 per kilogram — Karnataka growers have struggled to establish comparable brand recognition despite producing quality fruit across districts like Bengaluru Rural, Kolar, Chikkaballapura, Dharwad, and Ramanagara.

Recent seasons have brought additional pressure. Mango yields in Karnataka have faced significant declines. N. Chinnappa Reddy, president of the Kolar District Mango Growers Association, estimated a 35–40% drop in yield in a recent season, citing delayed flowering and thrips outbreaks. Scientists at the Indian Institute of Horticultural Research have warned that extreme temperatures and unseasonal rains compound the problem.

"Flowering was delayed until March in many areas, and the thrips outbreak worsened conditions. We expected 10 lakh tons but might only reach 5 lakh tons from Kolar's 32,000 acres."

— N. Chinnappa Reddy, President, Kolar District Mango Growers Association

A dedicated marketing platform could help Karnataka's Alphonso growers capture more value from their reduced harvests by connecting them with domestic buyers willing to pay premium prices for directly sourced, naturally ripened fruit — free from calcium carbide, which KSMDMC has made a point of guaranteeing through its existing channels.

Competition from Konkan and Beyond

The move puts KSMDMC in direct competition with organized efforts from Maharashtra's Konkan region. Platforms like MyKo, launched by Global Kokan with around 100 growers, and the Ekyaam brand, a partnership between Konkan farmers and Swiss-Indian food tech firm Innoterra involving over 2,000 growers, have been building premium Alphonso brands with GI tagging and QR-code traceability.

Former Union minister Suresh Prabhu has advocated for such branding efforts, stressing the need for geographical indication tags to protect farmer interests. Karnataka's entry into dedicated Alphonso marketing could reshape domestic competition and offer consumers more sourcing options.

What to Watch

The key questions remain: whether the new platform will operate as an extension of Karsiri or as a standalone marketplace, how it will handle logistics beyond the existing India Post partnership, and whether it can build the kind of brand trust that Konkan Alphonso already commands. For NRIs who eagerly await mango season each year and navigate complicated international shipping to get Alphonso delivered abroad, a more robust domestic infrastructure could eventually open new pathways for overseas direct sales — though that remains a longer-term prospect.
nri_angle: NRI mango lovers who rely on seasonal Alphonso shipments could benefit from a more organized domestic supply chain that may eventually expand to international direct-to-consumer sales.
